proposals.name: The Lamplighters' Guild
proposals.entry:
The Chartered Guild of Municipal Lamplighters keeps Fogport lit. Its members climb ladders into the fog with hooked poles, oil cans, replacement wicks, cleaning rags, and long-handled snuffers, lighting the city’s public lamps one by one each evening.

The Guild’s office occupies part of the stone plinth beneath Saint Orra’s Colossus in Lastlight, beside the public shrine, a tea stall, and the lost-property counter. The Guild has maintained the lamp in Orra’s raised hand for generations, though nobody agrees whether it is a ceremonial light, a civic mechanism, or something older.

Badge and Authority

Guild members wear dark, weatherproof coats and carry official brass lamp-pins on crimson-and-gold ribbons. The pin grants them the right to enter lamp houses, climb civic ladders, cross certain rooftops, and demand assistance from municipal guards. In practice, the badge is respected mostly by old people, sailors, tram conductors, and anyone who has ever been lost in Fogport after dark.

The Coming Darkness

For generations, Fogport relied on gas lamps, oil lamps, whale-oil lanterns, and other forms of flame. The Guild maintained them all.

That is changing. The Civic Order has begun replacing traditional street lamps with electric bulbs. Each year, another district is wired. Each new electrical grid means fewer lamps to tend, fewer ladders to climb, fewer apprentices to train, and fewer Guild members drawing a municipal wage.

The official explanation is progress. Electric lighting is cheaper, cleaner, brighter, and easier to control. Vauntin Quell presents the electrification of Fogport as proof that the city is entering the modern age.

The Lamplighters see something else: an entire profession being quietly dismantled.

The Guild has submitted formal petitions to Vauntin Quell asking for transitional wages, retraining, pensions, and protection for its oldest members. Their pleas have been recorded, stamped, filed, acknowledged, and ignored.

Every year, more districts go dark to the Guild.

The Work

A lamplighter’s duties include lighting public lamps at dusk, extinguishing them at dawn, cleaning soot from glass and reflectors, replacing wicks and fittings, refilling oil and gas reservoirs, repairing damaged lamp posts, reporting broken streets and suspicious activity, escorting the lost through dangerous fog, and maintaining emergency lamps during floods, fires, riots, and power failures.

The Guild insists that lighting is not merely maintenance. It is a public trust. A lamp tells a person where the street is. It marks the edge of the harbor, the mouth of an alley, the entrance to a station, or the way back home.

Internal Divisions

The Old Wickmen believe the electric bulbs are temporary and will eventually fail. They want the Guild to preserve its records and remain ready for the city’s return to flame.

The Practical School wants to retrain lamplighters as electricians, wiremen, and municipal engineers. They argue that a guild that refuses to change will become a museum.

The Orra Loyalists believe old lamps possess a civic and spiritual purpose that electricity cannot replace. They tend shrines, preserve old ceremonies, and keep extra lamps burning beneath Saint Orra’s Colossus.

The Night Walkers continue lighting unassigned lamps after the Civic Order has shut them down. Some work illegally. Others insist that the lamps themselves call them.

Old Vesper

Old Vesper is the Guild’s most famous living member, though he is no longer officially employed. He claims to have lit Fogport’s first gas lamp and the last lamp before the Catastrophe. He now carries a ladder through the fog, tending lights that have no visible posts and no place on any municipal map.

The Civic Vigilance calls this trespass. The Lamplighters’ Guild calls it none of their business. The lamps continue to burn.

The Blind Lamplighters

The Guild strongly denies any connection to the Blind Lamplighters, a dangerous splinter group that believes ordinary illumination hides deeper truths. They extinguish whole streets before robberies, sacrifices, disappearances, and other private ceremonies. Their members are known to infiltrate lamp depots and dark tram stops.

Some Guild members believe the Blind Lamplighters are criminals exploiting old Guild routes. Others believe they are former lamplighters who discovered something about the city’s lights and were driven underground.

posts.name: Gamemaster Only
posts.entry:
Vauntin Quell is personally responsible for the speed of Fogport’s electrification. He has publicly presented the project as modernization. Privately, his primary motive is cost reduction. Electric bulbs require fewer workers, fewer deliveries, fewer repairs, and less municipal oversight. The savings will be substantial.

The project also allows Quell to present himself as the ruler who dragged Fogport into the modern age. Every newly wired district becomes another monument to his administration.

The petitions from the Lamplighters’ Guild have never reached him in meaningful form. They are intercepted, summarized, delayed, or buried by Civic Order clerks before they reach his desk.

Quell knows the Guild is being destroyed. He considers this unfortunate but necessary.

There is one complication: the electric bulbs do not behave properly in every district. Some burn too brightly. Some fail whenever Saint Orra’s lamp is lit. Some reveal things in the fog that gaslight never did.

And in districts where the old lamps have been removed, faint amber lights still appear at night.
